this plant grows on the bottom of the mountain.

this plant is fruiting. the berries are edible. there may be medicinal uses for the leaves and barks.

this plant can be confused with the big leaf maple (acer macrophyllum) because its leaves have different shapes when they are young to mature. mature leaves of this plant resemble the shape of maple leaves. it also have a smooth underside much like maple. maples also grow in this location.

the underside of the leaves of the western sycamore (platanus racemos) is fuzzy. sycamore does not grow in this location.

california bay (umbellularia californica), sticky snakeroot (ageratina adenophora) and poison oak (toxicodendron diversilobum) grow on the upper mountain slopes in this location.

live canyon oak (quercus chrysolepis) and big leaf maple (acer macrophyllum) grow on the lower mountain slopes in this location.

 margins have larger, more rounded teeth;  on the underside of the leaf, the main veins are more prominent.
*  bark has thick ridges with exposed inner bark
*  fruit measures 1/2 to 3/4 inch long; fruit of red mulberry is generally >1 inch;  fruit is red at this time, but may turn purple when fully ripe.  There is a common misconception that it is white, but that is rarely true.

White Mulberry (Morus alba)

June 11, 2019
William B. Ide Adobe State Historic Park
Red Bluff, Tehama County, California
